label: Sundial Diagrams ('A trewe Est & weste erecte diall')
desc: Pen-and-ink technical drawings of sundial plates and gnomon styles, labelled 'Stile', 'A trewe Est & weste erecte diall', and 'Another fassion Stile...', flanked by the signature of Henry Dingley.

label: Sundial / Astronomical Quadrant Diagram
desc: Pen-and-ink radiating hour-line diagram with semicircular base marked '12', 11 radiating lines labelled with Roman numerals (VI, V, IIII, III, II, I, IX/XII, XI, X, IX, VIII, VII, VI) and Arabic numerals (1-6), plus 'sole' and 'Zenith'.

label: Dineley Coat of Arms (1613)
desc: Small pen-and-ink heraldic shield at bottom left: Argent, a fess (chequy/embattled) sable, in chief a mullet between two roundels (arms of Dineley / Dingley).

label: Perpetual Easter Table (Pryme 1-19 / Dominical Letters A-G)
desc: Ruled 20-row by 9-column pen-and-ink table giving Easter Day dates for Golden Numbers ('Pryme') 1-19 and Dominical Letters A-G.

label: Table of Weeks between Christmas and Shrove Sunday
desc: Ruled 21-row by 8-column table ('Pryme' 1-19 vs. Dominical Letters A-G / 0-6) showing the number of weeks between Christmas and Shrove Sunday.

label: Vertical Easter Table ('Ester for Euer')
desc: Narrow 3-column table ('Prym | Dom lett'r | Day Ester') covering March 21 to April 18.

label: Solar Cycle & Dominical Letter Table (1645-1668)
desc: Three-tier horizontal table giving Anno Domini, Prime/Cycle (1-28), and Dominical Letters from 1645 to 1668.

label: Red Chalk/Ochre Smear
desc: Broad diagonal strokes of red chalk/ochre pigment across the upper left quadrant of the page.

label: Fishing Plumb & Quill Float Diagrams
desc: Two small pen-and-ink diagrams in the left margin illustrating lead plumbs: 'a plo[m]be w[i]t[h]out a quill' and 'a plu[m]be w[i]t[h] a quill'.

label: Fishing Rod / Float Drawings
desc: Two pen-and-ink drawings at the foot of the left column depicting a vertical tapered rod/float joint and a horizontal ringed/tapered ferrule or float.

label: Parchment-Covered Drinking Glass for Toothache Smoke
desc: Small pen-and-ink sketch at the bottom right showing a drinking glass covered with parchment, used with a tobacco pipe to condense smoke into oil for toothache.

label: Surgical Pipe Diagram ('A Pype to heale thrustes')
desc: Pen-and-ink drawing of a flared surgical pipe/cannula with a small side eyelet, captioned above: 'A Pype to heale thrustes pa 71 of my owne invencion . & in Box it will not bee muche Bygger in Lengthe 6 ins'.

label: Marginal Manicule
desc: Small pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the lower-left margin beside 'Ad ulcera mala tibiarum pulchrum'.

label: Tipped-in Paper Slip (Closed)
desc: Small rectangular paper slip tipped into the right column of p. 21, bearing two additional recipes ('allom flox & camfer or olde Soore...') and covering 'Ad ulcera antiqua' beneath it (revealed in Canvas 61).

label: Tipped-in Slip Lifted with Metal Spatula
desc: A metal conservation spatula holds the tipped-in paper slip folded to the left, exposing the underlying recipe 'Ad ulcera antiqua' in the right column.

label: Tent and Plaster Pattern ('a.' and 'B.')
desc: Pen-and-ink diagram of a trapezoidal piece of plaster ('a.') ready to roll a tent, alongside the finished rolled tent ('B.') with three turned-out ends at the mouth of the hole to pluck it out by.

label: Incised Quill Tent Diagrams
desc: Two pen-and-ink drawings of a goose quill cut at the great end into six or more slits so it may lie flat as a linen tent, used in the 1613 hand-fistula case.

label: Margin Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand in the intercolumnar margin pointing to 'Vnguentum viride leniter fistulam mortificat' (Master Arderne's green ointment).

label: Bottom Margin Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand in the lower left margin pointing to 'An Exelent probe' made of dried beef sinew.

label: Upper Margin Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand in the right margin pointing to 'Nota . the probe made of a thumbe maye haue an eye in the greter end'.

label: Lower Margin Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand in the right margin pointing to 'I haue obserued that althoughe ye Sublimate be painefull...'.

label: Tent Made and Tent Unmade Diagrams
desc: Two pen-and-ink drawings at the foot of the right column showing a rolled tent with turned-out ends ('y^e tent made') and the flat notched/slit plaster pattern ('the tente vn made').

label: Marginal Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the left margin directing attention to the woodbine note ('ad. ʒiã : pun the small leaues of woodbynd...').

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the left margin of the right column, drawing attention to the clinical note on applying corrosives early in the morning ('Note yt when this & such other corrosiues are vsed...').

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the right margin of the right column beside 'ffor the same vid pa: 63:'.

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the left margin at the top of p. 44, pointing to the note 'Looke in pa. 188. take notte of ye Escar'.

label: Iron Stirring Tool Diagram
desc: Small inline pen-and-ink drawing of an iron tool with a hole on a staff ('an yorne w[i]t[h] hole on a staffe') used to stir molten lead into powder in 'To make cleane leade into pulder' (Mr. Sadler).

label: Marginal Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the left margin directed toward the heading 'ffor an vlcer mr Drayer'.

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the left margin pointing to 'An Exelent plaster' and the note on a broken shin just above it.

label: Marginal Manicule
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the right margin pointing to the 'Aliter' receipt using linen cloth wet in frog spawn and dried in the sun.

label: Harelip Suture Knot Diagram 1
desc: Pen-and-ink diagram in the right margin showing the figure-of-eight thread winding around the surgical needle for harelip repair.

label: Harelip Suture Knot Diagram 2
desc: Second pen-and-ink diagram in the right margin showing the double-loop suture winding around the needle.

label: Dry-Stitching Triangular Plasters
desc: Pen-and-ink diagram of two hatched three-square (triangular) linen plasters laced together across a wound with double thread.

label: Round-Headed Suture Pins
desc: Pen-and-ink diagram of two circular/cross-headed surgical pins or clasps used for wound closure.

label: Bandaged Legs (Dry Stitching)
desc: Pen-and-ink anatomical drawing of two human legs (frontal and profile views) illustrating dry-stitching plasters and roller bandages applied to the calf and shin.

label: Glyster Pipe / Wound Syringe
desc: Pen-and-ink drawing of a small tapered glyster pipe / cannula used to inject warm alkanet wound oil deep into narrow thrust wounds.

label: Marginal Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the right margin pointing left toward 'Digestiu[m] et faciens nasci carnem'.

label: Wooden Box ('ye Box')
desc: Pen-and-ink drawing of a cylindrical lidded wooden box with cross-hatched shading, labelled 'ye Box', illustrating the vessel used to shake and sift the lead and chalk powder.

label: Wooden Mortar ('ye morter')
desc: Pen-and-ink drawing of a deep cylindrical wooden mortar with cross-hatched shading, labelled 'ye morter', illustrating the thick-bottomed mortar described in the text.

label: Manicule (Left Margin, Upper)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the left margin pointing to the Sanatiuum receipt ('℞ Cice in Juyse Berorum...').

label: Manicule (Left Margin, Lower)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the left margin pointing to the note on the white plaster and alum water.

label: Manicule pointing to 1629 Broken Shin Note
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) at bottom right margin pointing left toward the dated clinical note 'Nota: R.D. hauing a Broken Shinn long in healinge ... Aprill 1629.'

label: Manicule pointing to 'A plastor to drye and heale'
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the outer left margin pointing right toward 'CC 4. Sallet oile ʒ iij yellow wax...' under 'A plastor to drye and heale'.

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the left margin beside the note on purging the stomach ('used to purge the Stomake w[i]t[h] Sum purgaton or pille').

label: Pointing Hand (Manicule)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the right column pointing to the note 'ut in pa 139. so well but make water, and dab it for proude flesh'.

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the left margin of column 2, drawing attention to the receipt for 'Agrimony water' / 'Doctor Butlers water'.

label: Manicule ('Brestes')
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the lower left margin beneath 'Brestes', directing attention to the full-width receipt for a sore breast at the foot of the page.

label: Manicule (30-40 Years' Practice Note)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the left margin pointing to the practitioner's empirical observation: 'After xxx or xl yeares practis, I found that the often changing the plaster did hinder the cure...'

label: Small Manicule (End of Left Column)
desc: Small pen-and-ink pointing hand at the bottom right of the left column next to 'wth iij or iv plasters finished the cure.'

label: Marginal Manicule
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the left margin pointing to 'ffor ache and Spraines'.

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the left margin pointing to 'An Exelent playster for the Gowte'.

label: Standing Male Figure Wearing Hernia Truss
desc: Pen-and-ink full-length drawing of a standing man wearing the cross-shoulder and groin hernia truss described in 'An Easy trusse & good', flanked by explanatory text.

label: Labelled Hernia Truss Technical Diagram
desc: Pen-and-ink technical diagram of the hernia truss laid flat, showing waist band (:a to :B:), shoulder straps (k, l), leg straps (c, d), stay (e, e), pad for broken side (f), and pad for whole side (h, i).

label: Pointing Manicule (Left Margin)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the left margin drawing attention to the note on preparing calcined marrow bones ('Take mary Bone Burnt is called ossa Cremosa').

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the left margin pointing to 'Many think this dysease is the hardnes of the Spleene'.

label: Marginal Manicule
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the right margin beside 'Pillule in collica G. D. Bauariæ', directing attention to the pill dosage.

label: Marginal Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the central gutter margin between columns, pointing right to the dated February 1629/30 case note of J. W.

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Small pen-and-ink manicule in the left margin of the right column pointing to the astrological timing note for worm medicines ('All medicines geven for the wormes must be geven...').

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink manicule in the right margin pointing to the receipt 'To kill wormes in children' (ivory shaven on oak leaves, walnut distillation).

label: Boxwood Ear-Fume Pipe Diagram
desc: Small pen-and-ink drawing of a slender turned boxwood pipe or funnel ('for a pype pa: 71 made of Box nott muche bigger then this picture'), used to channel steam from boiled mallows in an earthen pot into the ear.

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink manicule (pointing hand) in the left margin of the left column at the foot of the page, highlighting the note on keeping copperas in a parchment- and lead-covered glass.

label: Alchemical Diagram for Aurum Potabile
desc: Concentric circular pen-and-ink diagram in the right column. Center: 'ignis contra natura[m]'. Inner ring quadrants: 'A', 'B', 'C', 'D'. Outer ring quadrants: 'marcasita solis mall[eata]' (A), 'Succu[s] lunarie' (B), 'Sulphur Rubrum.' (C), 'materia arge[n]tea' (D).

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink manicule (pointing hand) in the lower right column pointing to the clinical note 'I did geve this medicyne that doth next followe for all agues hott and colde...'.

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the right margin beside the August 1623 note on colouring distilled water with red rose leaves.

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink pointing hand (manicule) in the center gutter beside the end of 'A ptizan for the cough'.

label: Splinted Lower Leg and Foot
desc: Pen-and-ink anatomical drawing of a lower leg and foot bound in splints and bandages, with a cross-mark '+' at left and 'vide 297.' above.

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Small pen-and-ink pointing hand at the bottom right beside 'Looke on the & on the next in the ende at'.

label: Manicule (Pointing Hand)
desc: Pen-and-ink manicule (pointing hand) in the intercolumnar margin pointing to the Latin note on Osteocolla near Heidelberg and Jena ('Item prope Heidelburgam ac Jenam Saxonie').

label: Unfinished 20-Quartering Heraldic Achievement Cartouche
desc: Large pen-and-ink and yellow-ochre wash Renaissance strapwork cartouche enclosing a 5-column by 4-row grid of 20 quarterings. Most quarters are blank; tricked pen-and-ink charges appear in Row 1 Col 2 (two engrailed bendlets), Row 1 Col 4 (two lions passant in pale with a crescent in sinister chief), Row 2 Col 1 (three chess rooks, 2 and 1), Row 2 Col 2 (a saltire engrailed between four mullets), Row 2 Col 4 (two faint diagonal strokes), Row 3 Col 1 (a voided cross with a faint sketch in sinister chief), and Row 3 Col 4 (a lion rampant), with occasional red tricking dots.

label: Armorial Grid: 30 Emblazoned Shields (Ordinary of Crosses)
desc: Six rows of five painted coats of arms (30 shields total), each featuring a cross (plain, ermine, checky, bendy, or charged with annulets, mullets, martlets, fleurs-de-lis, cinquefoils, or labels), with family names inscribed above each shield.

label: Armorial Grid: 8 Emblazoned Shields & 22 Blank Shield Outlines
desc: Six rows of five shield outlines (30 total): Row 1 (5 shields) and Row 2 cols 1-3 (3 shields) are painted with crosses and labelled; the remaining 22 shields are blank pencil outlines awaiting emblazonment.

desc: Row 1 (L-R): [Unlabelled] Argent a cross Gules charged with 5 mullets Argent; Aboloyne (Argent a cross Sable charged with 5 eagles displayed Argent); Birlingham (Or a cross Gules charged with 5 fleurs-de-lis Argent); Boynton (Or a cross Sable charged with 5 bull's heads erased Argent); Bygod (Or a cross Gules charged with 5 plates).

desc: Row 2 (L-R): [Unlabelled] Or a cross Gules charged with 5 escallops Argent; Cornwall devon (Argent a cross Sable charged with 5 bezants); Criktoftes (Azure a cross Argent charged with 5 escallops Gules); Durtynt Essex (blank outline); Digges kent (Gules a cross Argent charged with 5 eagles displayed Sable).

desc: Row 3 (L-R): Ellis (Or a cross Sable charged with 5 crescents Argent); fronyll wig (Or a cross Gules charged with 4 lozenges Argent and 1 lozenge vair); Lincolne (Argent a cross Azure charged with 5 estoiles Or); Lacer (Or a cross Azure charged with 5 roses Argent); newent (Sable a cross Argent charged with 5 eagles displayed Sable).

label: Armorial Shields Row 6 (5 blank shield outlines)
desc: Row 6 (L-R): Five blank unlabelled shield outlines.

label: Armorial Shields Row 1 (5 emblazoned shields)

(Or on a cross Sable between 4 oak leaves Vert 5 mullets Argent); Coggeshall Essex (Argent a cross Sable between 4 escallops Sable).

(Gules a cross Or between 4 groups of 3 cross-crosslets Or); flammocke corn (Argent a cross Gules between 4 mullets Gules pierced Or); Flyed (Argent on a cross Or 6 gouttes de sang between 4 birds Argent); Flote (Argent a cross Gules between 4 suns Gules); kingston (blank/unpainted).

desc: Row 6 (L-R): Five blank unlabelled shield outlines.

label: FitzAlan Earls of Arundel Pedigree Diagram (Part 1)
desc: Pen-and-ink genealogical tree of 24 circular roundels (one empty double-rimmed roundel at top, 23 inscribed roundels) linked by parallel marriage bars and descent lines, with a hatched continuation line below Richard Beauchamp leading to Canvas 402.

label: Armorial Shields Row 1 (4 emblazoned shields, 1 blank outline)
desc: Row 1 (L-R): Alleyne of Raley essex (Argent, a chevron Purpure charged with three crescents Argent between three talbots Sable); Alleyn thaxsted essex (Or, three pellets each charged with a lion passant Or, on a chief Gules a lion passant between two anchors Or); Alyef kent (Sable, a lion rampant Argent between three crosses formy Or within a bordure gobony Argent and Gules); Ammarle (blank shield outline); Anmarle (Argent, three bars Purpure surrounded by flames Gules).

label: FitzAlan Earls of Arundel Pedigree Diagram (Part 2)
desc: Pen-and-ink genealogical tree of 16 circular roundels (15 inscribed, 1 empty) linked by parallel marriage bars and descent lines, continuing the Arundel and Beauchamp/Neville lines from Canvas 400.

label: Armorial Shields Row 1 (5 emblazoned shields)
desc: Row 1 (L-R): Appulbye (Argent a bend Sable charged with 3 plates); Alebaster (Argent/Ermine a crossbow bent Gules among ermine spots/flies); Arsake (Gules a bend Or between 2 cotises Argent); Arden Ches: lan: (Gules 3 crosses crosslet fitchée Or, a chief indented Or); Arwod: uel: harwod (Argent 3 hares courant proper).
